sources.name: OME-NGFF 0.4 specification report
sources.locator: §3.1 axes; §3.3 coordinate transformations; §3.4 multiscales; §3.5 omero display metadata; §§3.6–3.7 labels and image-labels
sources.applicability: Axis names/types/units, array-axis correspondence, scale and translation transform order, multiscale layout and label representation inform the project/interchange contract.
sources.limits: The 0.4 report permits scale and translation coordinate transforms, not a general arbitrary affine; transitional fields and the report status do not promise compatibility with every implementation. Label groups address raster labels, not all vector/project semantics.

sources.name: Zarr-Python arrays user guide
sources.pin: Stable documentation captured alongside Zarr-Python v3.4.0 release on 2026-10-06; version inferred from contemporaneous stable release/docs state
sources.locator: User guide sections on chunked arrays, indexing/slicing, persistent stores, and reading/writing arrays; exact page headings: Basic indexing; Chunking; Persistent arrays
sources.applicability: Documents chunk subdivision and requested slicing into NumPy arrays; supports the bounded-region access design and persistent chunk-store option.
sources.limits: A slicing API does not establish actual decoder granularity, memory use or latency for a source format or integrated viewer. A full slice can materialize the complete array. The stable URL can move; use the recorded release and recapture before implementation lock.

sources.name: Zarr-Python v3 migration guide
sources.pin: Stable documentation captured alongside Zarr-Python v3.4.0 release on 2026-10-06
sources.locator: Sections on supported Zarr formats, default format for new arrays, zarr_format/default_zarr_format creation arguments, and API changes
sources.applicability: Zarr-Python 3 supports Zarr format v2 and v3; new arrays default to v3, while explicit zarr_format=2 or default_zarr_format=2 selects v2. Relevant to NGFF 0.4 implementation compatibility and pinning.
sources.limits: Migration guidance does not prove a particular OME-NGFF writer/reader combination interoperates. Validate the chosen library versions and artifact.

sources.name: tifffile v2026.9.20 release
sources.locator: Release body sections describing read-as-array or Zarr-array/group access and supported TIFF storage/series structures; release note fix for LSM >4GB offset unwrapping
sources.applicability: A candidate TIFF reader mechanism; notes reads from strips, tiles, pages/IFDs, SubIFDs, higher-order series and pyramid levels, with format/codec-specific capabilities.
sources.limits: Release notes and format list do not qualify every format/codec or prove lazy end-to-end access, bounded memory, or the proposed 3 GB target. The noted LSM fix is not used as an issue-to-test history because that chain was not independently established here.

sources.name: napari v0.9.0 release
sources.locator: Release notes describing multidimensional viewer stack, xarray scale/unit handling, float status coordinates, 2D multiscale chunk-aware loading and Zarr/Dask lazy multiscale; release classification as Macro under EffVer
sources.applicability: Supports considering napari as an existing multidimensional viewer/layer component and motivates exact version pinning.
sources.limits: Release notes do not demonstrate this proposal's import, project persistence, 3 GB memory, latency, coordinate round-trip or export behavior. Macro release may include API changes.

sources.name: Bio-Formats 8.4.0 supported formats
sources.pin: Bio-Formats v8.4.0 documentation; requested URL redirects to bio-formats.readthedocs.io/en/v8.4.0/supported-formats.html
sources.locator: Per-format support table and ratings for pixels, metadata, openness, presence, utility, export, license, multi-image and pyramid properties
sources.applicability: A bounded alternative reader for selected instrument formats after corpus-based testing; table is useful for identifying format-specific capabilities.
sources.limits: Broad format listing is not universal compatibility evidence and does not establish Python integration, memory or performance for the proposed application.

sources.name: SQLite Atomic Commit in SQLite
sources.pin: SQLite online documentation, last modified 2026-09-11; captured 2026-10-06
sources.locator: Atomic commit/rollback behavior and assumptions about OS, filesystem, hardware flush and power failure; article focuses on rollback-journal mode
sources.applicability: Supports transactional grouping of project edits and explains assumptions behind durable commit.
sources.limits: SQLite's documented atomicity depends on the stated platform and storage assumptions; it is not a guarantee for arbitrary shared storage or hardware. WAL behavior is addressed separately in S11.

sources.name: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.locator: WAL concurrency requirements; explicit network filesystem limitation; WAL/SHM files and checkpoint/close behavior
sources.applicability: Supports local working database and closed snapshot exchange; warns that a WAL database's related files can be persistent state and WAL mode does not work over a network filesystem.
sources.limits: Does not establish behavior on the group's particular SMB/shared storage or application recovery implementation; that must be tested.
